verdicts.A: fail (2/4: nominal_2 steering_feedback_stale, nominal_3 link_ttl_expired, both after one executor input stall of about 0.35 s SIM right after the start)
verdicts.B: fail (3/6: the first run refused the screen session with session_conflict; screen STOP and the restart after the STOP pass)
verdicts.C: pass (4/4 bridge_stall; start yaw rate 0.005-0.069 deg/s in every run)
verdicts.F: pass (3/3 row_end with the user local commands)

causes.A: executor side: the ROS input of the executor container (/clock, scan and IMU on one spin thread) stopped for about 0.35 s and came in at once (the SIM clock of the executor jumped, 5 and 9 ticks skipped); RTF 1.035 and 1.016, the check node got /clock without gaps (wall gap max 46 and 38 ms), host CPU about 30 %, the executor HTTP answered the 100 ms heartbeats at 0.100-0.104 s; DDS delivery or rclpy spin not separated. Not SIM resource or RTF, not the bridge, not the judge
causes.B: session_conflict on the first run: another operator session was bound and fresh while run 1 was open (270 heartbeats and one go of the screen refused); whose session is not recorded. Not SIM resource or RTF
causes.C: cause rule of the registration: no failing run, every run without a start offset passed; the stage 3 failure is put on the start yaw rate offset, which did not appear in these four runs

stage4.reruns: none: section 6 allows one more run only after a SIM side fix written first as an amendment; no SIM side fix was identified (and no RTF below 0.5)
